# `scripts/ops/`

## `scripts/ops/alerts.gd`

class_name `OpsAlerts` · extends `Node`

Local alerting. Every interval_s it evaluates res://data/alert_rules.json against live inputs: frame time p95, the GMI circuit breaker, the GMI live failure ratio, errors per minute (from ErrorTracker's in-memory counters) and sim tick stalls. A rule that fires (at most once per its cooldown_s) prints "OPS_ALERT {json}", is appended to user://ops/alerts.jsonl when error tracking or analytics records to disk, and becomes a player toast only when the "ops_alerts" flag is on and GRIDFALL_OPS_ALERTS_UI=1. The "ops_alerts" flag off disables evaluation. Also installs ErrorTracker and keeps its game context current.

### Signals

- `alert_fired(alert: Dictionary)`

### Constants

- `RULES_PATH = "res://data/alert_rules.json"`
- `FILE = "alerts.jsonl"`
- `FRAME_SAMPLES = 240`
- `MAX_FIRED = 50`

### Properties

- `main: Node`: The Main node (main.gd); sim, client and view_mode are read from it. May be null.
- `fired: Array[Dictionary]`: The most recent fired alerts (newest last).

### Functions

- `func tick(now_ms: int = -1) -> Array[Dictionary]`: One evaluation round: refreshes the error context, gathers inputs, fires due rules.
- `func gather_inputs(now_ms: int) -> Dictionary`: Live inputs for evaluate().
- `func fire(hit: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: Prints, records and (debug only) toasts one alert. Returns the alert record.
- `static func load_rules(path: String) -> Dictionary`: {"interval_s", "warmup_s", "rules": [...]} from path ({} when missing or invalid).
- `static func evaluate(rule_list: Array, inputs: Dictionary) -> Array[Dictionary]`: Pure rule evaluation. inputs: {"frame_ms": Array[float], "breaker_state": String, "live_outcomes": Array[bool], "errors_last_minute": int, "sim_stall_ratio": float}. Returns one {"id", "kind", "severity", "value", "threshold", "message"} per rule whose condition holds (cooldowns are the caller's, see due()).
- `static func due(rule: Dictionary, last_fired: Dictionary, now_ms: int) -> bool`: True when rule may fire at now_ms given {id: last fired ms}.
- `static func percentile(values: Array, q: float) -> float`: The q-quantile (0..1, nearest rank) of values.

## `scripts/ops/analytics.gd`

class_name `Analytics` · extends `RefCounted`

Local, opt-in product analytics: track(event, props) appends {event, props, session, seq, ts, build} to user://ops/analytics.jsonl (scrubbed, rotated). On only with GRIDFALL_ANALYTICS=1 or the "analytics" flag; otherwise track() costs one breadcrumb check and one bool test. Nothing leaves the machine; tools/ops/analytics_report.py summarises the file. Props must not carry player text (send lengths, ids and counts instead).

### Constants

- `FILE = "analytics.jsonl"`

### Functions

- `static func enabled() -> bool`: GRIDFALL_ANALYTICS=1 or the "analytics" flag (resolved once; configure() overrides).
- `static func configure(on: bool) -> void`: Forces analytics on or off for this process (tests).
- `static func track(event: String, props: Dictionary = {}) -> void`: Records one product event. Also leaves an error-tracker breadcrumb.
- `static func uptime_s() -> float`: Seconds since the process started.

## `scripts/ops/circuit_breaker.gd`

class_name `CircuitBreaker` · extends `RefCounted`

Consecutive-failure circuit breaker. closed: calls pass; failure_threshold failures in a row open it. open: calls are refused for cooldown_ms. Then half_open: one probe call passes (the rest are refused until it reports); its success closes the breaker, its failure re-opens it. Every method takes an optional now_ms (Time.get_ticks_msec() when negative) so tests can drive the clock.

### Signals

- `state_changed(from: String, to: String)`

### Constants

- `CLOSED = "closed"`
- `OPEN = "open"`
- `HALF_OPEN = "half_open"`

### Properties

- `open_count: int`: How many times the breaker opened.

### Functions

- `func allow(now_ms: int = -1) -> bool`: True when a call may go out now. In half_open only the first caller gets true (the probe).
- `func record_success() -> void`
- `func record_failure(now_ms: int = -1) -> void`
- `func peek_state(now_ms: int = -1) -> String`: The state as a caller would see it now: an open breaker past its cooldown reads half_open.
- `func retry_in_ms(now_ms: int = -1) -> int`: Milliseconds until an open breaker lets a probe through (0 when not open).
- `func reset() -> void`

## `scripts/ops/error_tracker.gd`

class_name `ErrorTracker` · extends `Logger`

Contextual error tracking, registered with OS.add_logger(). Always counts errors and warnings in memory (OpsAlerts reads errors_in_last()); with file output on (GRIDFALL_ERROR_LOG=1 or the "error_tracking" flag) it also appends one JSON line per error to user://ops/errors.jsonl: fingerprint, scrubbed message, source location, build, session, game context, the last breadcrumbs and the script backtrace. Godot may call a Logger from any thread, so everything here goes through _mutex and nothing touches the scene tree; the main thread feeds context with set_context().

### Constants

- `FILE = "errors.jsonl"`
- `MAX_BREADCRUMBS = 20`
- `MAX_PER_FINGERPRINT = 25`: Further repeats of one fingerprint are only counted, so a per-frame error cannot fill the disk.
- `MAX_TIMES = 256`
- `TYPE_NAMES = ["error", "warning", "script", "shader"]`

### Functions

- `static func install(file_output: bool = file_wanted()) -> void`: Registers the logger once (main thread). file_output defaults to file_wanted().
- `static func uninstall() -> void`
- `static func installed() -> bool`
- `static func file_wanted() -> bool`: GRIDFALL_ERROR_LOG=1 or the "error_tracking" flag.
- `static func set_file_output(on: bool) -> void`
- `static func recording() -> bool`: True when errors are written to disk.
- `static func breadcrumb(text: String) -> void`: Records a short "what just happened" line attached to the next errors (kept only while recording).
- `static func set_context(patch: Dictionary) -> void`: Merges patch (view mode, sim day and tick, ...) into the context attached to each error.
- `static func errors_in_last(window_ms: int, now_ms: int = -1) -> int`: Errors (not warnings) captured in the last window_ms.
- `static func counts() -> Dictionary`: {"error": n, "warning": n} since start (or reset()).
- `static func reset() -> void`: Clears counters, breadcrumbs, context and the per-fingerprint caps (tests).
- `static func fingerprint(file: String, line: int, code: String) -> String`: Stable 16-hex id of an error site: file, line and the error code text.
- `static func capture(function: String, file: String, line: int, code: String, rationale: String, error_type: int, backtraces: Array = []) -> Dictionary`: Counts one error and, when recording, writes it. Returns the written record ({} when only counted). _log_error forwards here; tests call it directly.

## `scripts/ops/feature_flags.gd`

class_name `FeatureFlags` · extends `RefCounted`

Feature flags. Defaults and descriptions live in res://data/feature_flags.json; overrides come from user://feature_flags.json ({"name": bool}, skipped when GRIDFALL_FLAGS_IGNORE_USER=1) and then from GRIDFALL_FLAGS ("overview=0,analytics=1"). First-person features are flagged by their registry id (FpMode skips a disabled one); unknown names fall back to the caller's default.

### Constants

- `DEFAULTS_PATH = "res://data/feature_flags.json"`
- `USER_PATH = "user://feature_flags.json"`
- `TRUE_WORDS = ["1", "true", "on", "yes"]`
- `FALSE_WORDS = ["0", "false", "off", "no"]`

### Functions

- `static func enabled(flag: String, default: bool = true) -> bool`: Whether flag is on. default is used for a name no layer defines.
- `static func reload() -> void`: Re-reads every layer from the environment and disk.
- `static func load_layers(env_spec: String, use_user: bool) -> void`: Builds the flag table from the JSON defaults, the user file (when use_user) and env_spec.
- `static func set_override(flag: String, on: bool) -> void`: Sets one flag for this process (tests, debug consoles).
- `static func defaults() -> Dictionary`: {name: default} from res://data/feature_flags.json.
- `static func describe() -> Dictionary`: {name: {"default": bool, "description": String}} from res://data/feature_flags.json.
- `static func snapshot() -> Dictionary`: The current value of every known flag.
- `static func read_user(path: String) -> Dictionary`: {name: bool} from a user override file: {"name": bool|0|1} or {"flags": {...}}.
- `static func parse_overrides(spec: String) -> Dictionary`: Parses "a=0,b=1,c,!d" into {"a": false, "b": true, "c": true, "d": false}; bad items are skipped.

## `scripts/ops/gpu_memory.gd`

class_name `GpuMemory` · extends `RefCounted`

Low-GPU-memory mode. decide() reads the graphics card once per process (the RenderingServer's adapter name, vendor and type, then its memory from nvidia-smi on NVIDIA or from the amdgpu sysfs files on Linux) and turns the mode on for an integrated or software GPU, a card with 4 GB or less, or one with less than LOW_FREE_MIB free (another program, such as a local LLM server, holding the rest). apply_to() then shrinks what the renderer allocates before the city is built, and FpMode defaults the quality preset to Low. GRIDFALL_LOW_VRAM=1 or 0 forces the mode on or off; with the "low_vram_auto" flag off only that switch turns it on.

### Constants

- `LOW_TOTAL_MIB = 4608`: A "4 GB" card reports 4096 MiB (some a little less); the next common size is 6 GB.
- `LOW_FREE_MIB = 1536`
- `SUN_ATLAS = 4096`
- `LAMP_ATLAS = 2048`
- `SETTINGS = { "rendering/lights_and_shadows/directional_shadow/size": SUN_ATLAS, "rendering/lights_...`: Project values set for this process, so first person's render_opt restores to them on exit.
- `TRUE_WORDS = ["1", "true", "on", "yes"]`
- `FALSE_WORDS = ["0", "false", "off", "no"]`

### Functions

- `static func probe() -> Dictionary`: The card: {"adapter", "vendor", "type" (RenderingDevice.DeviceType), "total_mib", "free_mib", "source"}; memory is -1 when unknown (headless, or no tool reports it).
- `static func reason(info: Dictionary, env: String, auto: bool, web: bool = false) -> String`: Why the mode is on for this card, or "" when it is off. env is GRIDFALL_LOW_VRAM; auto is the "low_vram_auto" flag; web is the browser build, which always starts lean (WebGL 2 on whatever laptop opens the page, and it cannot read the card's memory), so it starts on Low too.
- `static func decide() -> Dictionary`: probe() with "low" and "reason", decided on the first call and cached for the process.
- `static func low() -> bool`: Whether the low-GPU-memory mode is on.
- `static func set_override(on: bool, why: String = "test") -> v`: Sets the decision for this process (tests); clear() forgets it.
- `static func clear() -> void`
- `static func apply_to(vp: Viewport) -> void`: Shrinks what the renderer allocates: the sun's shadow atlas 8192 -> 4096 and its filter, SSAO quality, MSAA off (FXAA instead) and the lamp shadow atlas of vp. Also sets SETTINGS as project values for this process (never saved).
- `static func compat(method: String) -> bool`: True for the Compatibility renderer's method name (gl_compatibility).
- `static func describe(info: Dictionary) -> String`: One line for the log: the card, its memory and the decision.
- `static func parse_nvidia(text: String) -> Array[Dictionary]`: Rows of `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total,memory.free --format=csv,noheader,nounits`: [{"name", "total_mib", "free_mib"}]; malformed lines are skipped.
- `static func pick_row(rows: Array[Dictionary], adapter: String) -> Dictionary`: The row whose name the adapter carries (several cards), else the first; {} when there is none.

## `scripts/ops/ops_sink.gd`

class_name `OpsSink` · extends `RefCounted`

Local JSON-lines files for the opt-in ops features (errors, analytics, alerts). Each record is scrubbed (Redact) before it is written; a file past max_bytes rotates to <name>.1.jsonl, so a stream never takes more than about twice its cap. Thread-safe (the error tracker writes from whatever thread raised the error).

### Constants

- `MAX_BYTES = 1_000_000`

### Properties

- `dir: String`: Output directory; tests point it at a scratch folder.

### Functions

- `static func path_of(file_name: String) -> String`
- `static func append(file_name: String, rec: Dictionary, max_bytes: int = MAX_BYTES) -> bool`: Appends rec as one scrubbed JSON line to dir/file_name. False when the file cannot be written.
- `static func read_all(file_name: String) -> Array[Dictionary]`: Every parsed record of dir/file_name (the live file only), oldest first.

## `scripts/ops/pack_loader.gd`

class_name `PackLoader` · extends `RefCounted`

Streams the web build's background packs: the boot pack is the engine's own `.pck`, and the others land later under `user://packs/`, each mounted with `ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack`. The engine loads the boot pack before any script runs, so the manifest that says which pack holds an asset rides inside it (`res://web_manifest.json`). A pack is cached in the browser's IDBFS under a name that carries its own content hash, so a repeat visit reuses it without a byte on the wire; a cached file whose size no longer matches its manifest entry is deleted and fetched again rather than failing the load. Desktop builds have no manifest and every method here is a no-op, so nothing changes there.

### Signals

- `pack_arrived(pack: String)`: Emitted once a pack is mounted and its resources are available.
- `pack_failed(pack: String, reason: String)`: Emitted after a failed attempt, with a reason code; the pack can be requested again.

### Constants

- `MANIFEST_PATH = "res://web_manifest.json"`
- `CACHE_DIR = "user://packs"`
- `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_S = 60.0`: Per-attempt ceiling for one pack download; the coordinator's watchdog enforces the policy, this is the transport-level backstop.

### Functions

- `func load_manifest() -> bool`: Reads the manifest the export wrote into the boot pack; false when this build is unsplit.
- `func manifest_status() -> String`: "none" (unsplit build), "invalid" (a manifest was there but unusable) or "ok".
- `func active() -> bool`: True when the export shipped a split pack set (and so the runtime should stream it).
- `func pack_of(path: String) -> String`: The pack that holds the asset at a res:// path, or "" when it rides in the boot pack.
- `func pack_names() -> PackedStringArray`: The packs the manifest declares (download order is the coordinator's business).
- `func active_pack() -> String`: The pack currently downloading/mounting, or "".
- `func mounted(pack: String) -> bool`: True once the pack is mounted and its assets can be loaded.
- `func pending(pack: String) -> bool`: True while the pack is on its way (queued, downloading or mounting).
- `func needed_for(path: String) -> String`: The pack a path needs, or "" when it is already available (in the boot pack or mounted).
- `func request(pack: String) -> bool`: Queues a pack (once). Call pump() to advance; returns false when the pack does not exist.
- `func request_next(pack: String) -> bool`: Queues a pack at the front (a consumer asked for an asset in it right now). Never touches the active transfer; returns false when the pack does not exist.
- `func cancel_active(reason: String = "cancelled")`: Cancels the active transfer, if any, emitting pack_failed with the given reason once.
- `func cache_path(pack: String) -> String`: Local cache path for a pack: its own content hash keeps a stale file from ever being reused.
- `func pump(host: Node) -> bool`: Advances the queue on a node (one download at a time). Returns true while work remains.
- `func progress() -> float`: Fraction of the background packs that are in (0..1); 1 when there is nothing to fetch.
- `func reset() -> void`: Drops the in-memory state (tests, and a scene reload).

## `scripts/ops/redact.gd`

class_name `Redact` · extends `RefCounted`

Masks secrets and personal data in text bound for logs and the local ops files: bearer and basic credentials, key=value secrets, sk- keys, JWTs, long random tokens, e-mail addresses and every value registered with add_secret() (the live GMI key).

### Constants

- `MASK = "[REDACTED]"`
- `MIN_SECRET = 8`: Registered secrets shorter than this are ignored (masking "abc" would shred normal text).
- `TOKEN_RUN = 20`: A token is masked when it holds an alphanumeric run this long with enough digits and letters.

### Functions

- `static func add_secret(secret: String) -> void`: Registers a value that must never reach a log (call once with the API key).
- `static func scrub(text: String, extra: PackedStringArray = PackedStringArray()) -> String`: text with every secret, credential and e-mail address masked. extra: more literal secrets.

## `scripts/ops/trace.gd`

class_name `Trace` · extends `RefCounted`

Request and trace ids. A trace groups the calls of one unit of work (the brain's day round): set it with begin() before the calls start and end() after; GmiClient stamps every request with its own request id plus the current trace id (X-Request-ID / X-Trace-ID headers, log records).

### Functions

- `static func new_id() -> String`: 16 lowercase hex chars from the system CSPRNG.
- `static func begin(label: String = "") -> String`: Starts a new current trace (label is for humans, e.g. "day 4") and returns its id.
- `static func end() -> void`: Clears the current trace.
- `static func set_current(id: String, label: String = "") -> void`: Makes id the current trace (to resume one across an await); "" clears it.
- `static func current() -> String`: The current trace id, "" when none.
- `static func current_label() -> String`
- `static func session_id() -> String`: One id per game process, shared by analytics, error and alert records.
- `static func is_id(s: String) -> bool`

## `scripts/ops/web_pack_stream.gd`

class_name `WebPackStream` · extends `Node`

Background-pack streaming policy for the split web build (ops layer). Owns the one PackLoader pump, the download order, bounded retries and the status snapshot the HUD shows. Created by Main on every platform but inert unless activate() succeeds: streaming needs the web_split_packs flag AND the web platform AND a validated manifest. A split build with the flag off is a configuration error (the boot pack cannot conjure the missing packs); roll a split release back by replacing it with the unsplit one, never by disabling the flag. Downloads continue while the pause menu stops the world (PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS); mounting the arrived packs refreshes geometry only through the normal render processing of the consumers.

### Signals

- `pack_ready(pack: String)`
- `state_changed(snapshot: Dictionary)`

### Constants

- `DEFAULT_ORDER = [ "midlod", "sky", "traffic", "people", "props", "wildlife", "posters", "audio" ]`: Default background order: midlod first (it ends runtime gather stalls), then the decorative packs. Packs absent from the manifest are skipped; unknown manifest packs queue last.
- `RETRY_DELAYS_S = [2.0, 8.0]`: Automatic retry backoff after the first attempt: two retries, after 2 and 8 seconds.
- `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S = 60.0`: One download attempt may take at most this long before the watchdog cancels it.

### Properties

- `force_platform`: Test seam: "web" makes the platform check pass off the web; never set in game code.

### Functions

- `func setup(loader: PackLoader, clock: Callable = Callable()) -> void`: Inject the loader and (tests only) a fake msec clock. Call before activate().
- `func loader_active() -> bool`: True when the embedded manifest is valid, whatever the flag says (a split build).
- `func activate() -> int`: Starts streaming when the flag, the platform and the manifest all allow it. See ACTIVATE_*.
- `func request_path(path: String) -> String`: The pack a path still needs, or "" when it is available. Demanding an unqueued pack moves it ahead of the queued optional packs, but never cancels the active transfer or leapfrogs midlod's first request; demands among themselves keep their arrival order. A failed pack stays failed (the retry budget is not resettable by consumers); the HUD uses retry_failed().
- `func mounted(pack: String) -> bool`: True once the pack's assets can be loaded.
- `func snapshot() -> Dictionary`: A point-in-time copy of the pack states for the HUD; safe to keep and diff.
- `func retry_failed() -> void`: The HUD's retry button: a fresh bounded cycle for failed packs only.

## `scripts/ops/web_support.gd`

class_name `WebSupport` · extends `RefCounted`

Platform glue for the web build. Desktop answers the thread questions with a plain yes and the browser store stays empty, so every guard here is a no-op there (gate quick is unchanged). The store is a thin localStorage bridge: values never pass through Godot logs, and the only thing the game ever stores is the player's own GMI API key, after they tick "Remember" (see GmiClient.remember_player_key()).

### Functions

- `static func threads_supported() -> bool`: True when real threads can start (desktop platforms and the threaded web build). A no-threads web build answers false, so its callers load synchronously instead. GRIDFALL_NO_THREADS=1 forces it off for tests.
- `static func is_web() -> bool`: True in the browser export.
- `static func store_get(name: String) -> String`: localStorage value under name ("" off the web, when missing, or when the browser blocks it).
- `static func store_set(name: String, value: String) -> void`: Writes value under name (no-op off the web).
- `static func store_erase(name: String) -> void`: Removes name from the store (no-op off the web).
